task_1.title: Add GCC 15.1 compiler support
task_1.description: The upgrade adds support for GCC 15.1 as a recognized compiler version so users can declare and consume packages with that toolchain in Conan 2.16.0. The change is limited to compiler-version support and keeps the existing GCC settings model and related behavior otherwise unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that GCC 15.1 is supported as a valid compiler version for Conan package settings so users can configure profiles and package builds with that compiler version without version-rejection errors.

expectation.grounded: Conan should accept `compiler=gcc` with `compiler.version=15.1` anywhere GCC compiler settings are validated from the default settings model. GCC 15.1 should participate in the existing GCC configuration surface without introducing new GCC-specific setting categories or changing the currently modeled standard-selection behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to select GCC 15.1 in Conan the same way they can select previously supported GCC versions. The upgrade should make GCC 15.1 a first-class supported compiler target while leaving the overall GCC configuration experience consistent with earlier releases.

constraints.grounded: Support is limited to recognizing GCC version 15.1 within the existing GCC settings schema. Existing GCC subsettings and previously supported GCC versions must remain valid, and the upgrade must not imply new behavior for unmodeled compiler defaults beyond current Conan support.
constraints.conceptual: The change should expand compatibility to GCC 15.1 without regressing existing GCC workflows or altering unrelated compiler-setting behavior.

behavior: GCC 15.1 is recognized as a supported `compiler.version` value for the GCC compiler.
Profiles, settings, or package configurations that declare GCC 15.1 are no longer rejected solely because that version was missing from the supported GCC version list.
The existing GCC settings surface remains the same apart from the added version support.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures Conan with `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=15.1`, the configuration should be accepted as a supported compiler version.
When a package or profile targets GCC 15.1, Conan should treat it as a normal GCC configuration rather than an unknown compiler-version value.
When users continue to target previously supported GCC versions, their configurations should behave as before.
When users rely on existing GCC-related settings, the upgrade should not require any new setting names or changed configuration structure.

task_2.title: Support multilib components in CMakeConfigDeps with deprecation warnings
task_2.description: Version 2.16.0 adds compatibility for Conan packages that declare multiple libraries inside a single component when generating CMake config dependencies. CMakeConfigDeps now accepts that package shape, preserves consumer linkability by normalizing it into single-library component dependencies internally, and emits a deprecation warning so package authors can migrate to one component per library.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.16.0 allows CMakeConfigDeps consumers to use packages whose cpp_info.components entries expose more than one library, while warning package authors that multi-library components are deprecated and should be modeled as one component per library.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps processes a Conan package whose cpp_info.components[<name>].libs contains multiple library names, dependency generation should succeed instead of rejecting or mishandling that component. The original component should remain consumable as an aggregate component, a deprecation warning should be emitted for that component definition, and the multiple libraries should be represented as individual single-library component dependencies for downstream CMake consumers.
expectation.conceptual: Packages that still group several libraries under one declared component should continue to work with generated CMake package configuration files after the upgrade. Consumers should be able to link the advertised component or package target and receive all underlying libraries, but authors should be clearly warned that this component shape is deprecated and should be split in the future.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing handling for packages with one library per component or for existing package-level multi-library compatibility. Preserve observable component consumption through CMakeConfigDeps, keep deprecation signaling for multi-library declarations, and normalize deprecated multi-library components into one-library dependency units during generation.
constraints.conceptual: The compatibility addition should be backward-compatible for consumers, limited to supporting a previously problematic deprecated component layout, and should not change the expected behavior of already-correct package and component definitions.

behavior: If a Conan component declares more than one entry in cpp_info.components[<name>].libs, CMakeConfigDeps should still generate usable dependency metadata for that package.
A deprecation warning should be emitted for each component that declares multiple libraries.
The declared component should behave as an aggregate component rather than as a direct multi-library unit during dependency generation.
Each library listed in a deprecated multi-library component should be surfaced as its own single-library dependency unit for CMake consumption.
Linking the package or component target produced by CMakeConfigDeps should continue to pull in all libraries that were previously grouped inside that component.
acceptance_criteria: When a package recipe defines cpp_info.components["core"].libs with two or more libraries and a consumer uses CMakeConfigDeps, dependency generation should complete and produce consumable CMake package metadata.

When such a package is consumed through its generated CMake targets, linking the exported package or component target should resolve all libraries declared under the deprecated multi-library component.
When a multi-library component is encountered, the package author should receive a deprecation warning indicating that one component per library is the supported model.
When a package already defines components with zero or one library each, upgrading to 2.16.0 should not change its observable CMakeConfigDeps consumption behavior.

task_3.title: Expose dependency CMake modules through CMakeConfigDeps
task_3.description: Conan 2.16.0 updates CMakeConfigDeps so CMake modules shipped by dependencies become discoverable through the normal include() workflow. Packages that publish module files in their declared build directories can now be consumed from both regular requirements and tool requirements without manually extending the module search path.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects using CMakeConfigDeps can include CMake modules provided by dependencies without manually managing the module search path.

expectation.grounded: CMakeConfigDeps should populate CMAKE_MODULE_PATH from dependency cpp_info.builddirs entries, using contributors from both host requirements and direct build requirements. After generation, CMake include(<module>) should be able to resolve module files stored in those packaged build directories. If no dependency exposes builddirs, no additional module-path contribution should be introduced.
expectation.conceptual: When a dependency or tool dependency ships reusable CMake modules, consumers using the generated CMake integration should be able to load those modules with normal include() calls, with no extra manual path wiring.

constraints.grounded: This change must be additive to existing CMakeConfigDeps path generation: program, library, include, and framework path behavior must remain intact, and only package-declared build directories should influence CMAKE_MODULE_PATH. Dependency-provided module paths should be added in a way that makes them available during configure time.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should expand module discovery without changing unrelated dependency lookup behavior or requiring consumers to change how they locate programs, libraries, headers, or frameworks.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps now exposes dependency build directories through CMAKE_MODULE_PATH.
Module path contributions are collected from both regular requirements and tool requirements.
CMake modules packaged by dependencies can be loaded through include(<module>) during project configuration.
If no dependency provides module directories, generated behavior for module lookup remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer uses CMakeConfigDeps and a regular requirement publishes a CMake module in its declared build directories, include(<module>) should resolve that module without manual CMAKE_MODULE_PATH edits.

When a consumer uses CMakeConfigDeps and a tool requirement publishes a CMake module in its declared build directories, include(<module>) should resolve that module without manual CMAKE_MODULE_PATH edits.
When dependencies do not publish build directories containing CMake modules, existing CMakeDeps-generated lookup behavior for other dependency assets should continue to work unchanged.
When dependency module paths are generated, they should be available during CMake configure-time module resolution.

task_4.title: Configurable audit scan severity threshold
task_4.description: The upgrade adds severity-threshold enforcement to `conan audit scan`, allowing vulnerability scans to fail when findings reach a configured CVSS level. The command now defaults to treating critical vulnerabilities as errors, which changes runtime behavior for users and CI flows while preserving the normal vulnerability report output.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan audit scan` supports a configurable vulnerability severity threshold and fails the command when scanned dependencies contain findings at or above that threshold, with critical findings causing failure by default.

expectation.grounded: `conan audit scan` must accept `-sl` / `--severity-level` as a float threshold for CVSS severity evaluation. After scanning, if any vulnerability in the returned audit data has `cvss.preferredBaseScore` greater than or equal to the configured threshold, the command result must be marked as `conan_error` so the command exits as a general error. The default threshold is `9.0`, so critical vulnerabilities fail the command by default. Threshold values above the CVSS maximum effectively disable threshold-triggered failure. Dependency-graph resolution failures for `conan audit scan` must also surface through `conan_error`.
expectation.conceptual: `conan audit scan` should let users define how severe a vulnerability must be before the scan is considered a failure. By default, critical vulnerabilities should make the command fail, but users should be able to raise the threshold to avoid failing on lower-severity findings or effectively disable this failure mode. The scan should still present the vulnerability results even when it fails.

constraints.grounded: The threshold-based failure applies to `conan audit scan` and must not suppress normal vulnerability reporting. Findings below the configured threshold must not turn a successful scan into an error. Existing audit error handling should remain consistent by using `conan_error` for scan-level failures, including dependency graph errors. The requirement should not assume any changes to `conan audit list`.
constraints.conceptual: Only scans that meet the configured severity cutoff should fail because of vulnerability severity. Regular scan output should remain available, and unrelated audit commands should not be implicitly changed by this requirement.

behavior: `conan audit scan` accepts a new `-sl` / `--severity-level` option for defining the CVSS score threshold that converts a scan into a failure.
If any discovered vulnerability has a CVSS preferred base score equal to or higher than the configured threshold, the scan is flagged as a command error.
The default threshold is `9.0`, so critical vulnerabilities now cause `conan audit scan` to fail unless the user overrides the threshold.
Setting the threshold above the CVSS scoring range prevents severity-based failure while still returning the vulnerability findings.
Dependency graph errors encountered before scanning are surfaced through the same audit error channel used for threshold-triggered scan failures.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan audit scan` without `--severity-level` and a dependency has a vulnerability with CVSS score `9.0` or higher, the command should return an error while still showing the vulnerability report.
When a user runs `conan audit scan --severity-level <value>` and all discovered vulnerabilities have CVSS scores below that value, the command should complete successfully and show the scan results.
When a discovered vulnerability has a CVSS score exactly equal to the configured `--severity-level`, the command should treat that as a failure condition.
When the user sets `--severity-level` above the maximum possible CVSS score, severity alone should not cause the scan to fail.
When `conan audit scan` cannot complete because dependency graph resolution fails, it should surface that condition as an audit command error.

task_6.title: Add CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM support
task_6.description: Conan now supports generating CycloneDX 1.6 SBOMs and aligns CycloneDX package typing with Conan application packages. The new output adopts the 1.6 schema for authors and tool metadata while preserving existing dependency selection and SBOM content where the schema did not change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can generate CycloneDX 1.6 SBOMs and that CycloneDX SBOM output correctly identifies application packages while reflecting the schema changes introduced in CycloneDX 1.6.

expectation.grounded: `conan.tools.sbom` should expose `cyclonedx_1_6` alongside `cyclonedx_1_4`. `cyclonedx_1_6(conanfile, name=None, add_build=False, add_tests=False, ...)` should generate a CycloneDX document with `specVersion` `1.6`, `bomFormat` `CycloneDX`, 1.6-style `metadata.tools` content, `authors` arrays instead of deprecated `author` fields, and component/metadata `type` values derived from Conan `package_type` (`application` or `library`). `cyclonedx_1_4(...)` should also derive `type` from `package_type` instead of always emitting `library`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to opt into CycloneDX 1.6 output and receive SBOMs that match the 1.6 schema, while both supported CycloneDX formats should accurately identify applications as applications rather than always treating them as libraries.

constraints.grounded: `add_build` and `add_tests` filtering semantics must remain intact, dependency relationships must continue to be emitted, and unchanged SBOM fields should keep their prior meaning. For 1.6 output, deprecated singular `author` fields must not be emitted, `authors` should only appear when author data exists, and optional entries such as licenses or external references should remain omitted when their source data is absent.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add the new schema support without changing which dependencies are included or regressing existing SBOM content outside the documented CycloneDX 1.6 differences.

behavior: `conan.tools.sbom` exports a new public generator named `cyclonedx_1_6`.
`cyclonedx_1_6` emits CycloneDX documents with `specVersion` `1.6` while retaining the standard CycloneDX document identity fields.
In CycloneDX 1.6 output, component and metadata author information is represented through `authors` arrays, and deprecated singular `author` fields are no longer used.
In CycloneDX 1.6 output, metadata tool information uses the newer structured tools/components shape and identifies Conan as the generating tool with version information.
For both `cyclonedx_1_4` and `cyclonedx_1_6`, component and metadata `type` values become `application` when the Conan package is an application; otherwise they remain `library`.

Dependency entries continue to reflect the selected host/build/test graph, and 1.6 output preserves existing component metadata such as name, version, purl, description, homepage-derived references, and licenses when those values exist.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer imports `cyclonedx_1_6` from `conan.tools.sbom` and generates an SBOM, it should produce a CycloneDX document whose schema version is 1.6.

When a recipe provides author information and `cyclonedx_1_6` is used, the generated SBOM should expose that information through `authors` fields for metadata and components; when no author is provided, it should not emit deprecated singular `author` fields.
When a package declares itself as an application, both `cyclonedx_1_4` and `cyclonedx_1_6` should mark the relevant SBOM component type as `application` rather than `library`.
When `cyclonedx_1_6` includes generator metadata, it should describe the producing Conan tool using the CycloneDX 1.6 tools structure and include tool version information.
When build or test dependencies are excluded through `add_build` or `add_tests`, the generated components and dependency relationships should continue to honor those filters.

task_5.title: Align GnuToolchain with recent Autotools and Android cross-build behavior
task_5.description: The upgrade extends GnuToolchain with recent AutotoolsToolchain behavior, improving Apple flag propagation and Android cross-build environment generation while preserving user-defined build environment compiler settings.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.16.0 makes `GnuToolchain` mirror the latest `AutotoolsToolchain` behavior for Apple builds and cross-builds: preserve Apple-specific extra flags, configure Android NDK host tools more completely, avoid overwriting user-provided build-environment compilers, and continue exposing build-machine compilers separately during cross-building.

expectation.grounded: `GnuToolchain` generation should include the same Apple extra flag handling used by `AutotoolsToolchain`, applying relevant `tools.apple` configuration to generated `CFLAGS`, `CXXFLAGS`, and `LDFLAGS`. For Android cross-builds, it should infer the host triplet from `settings.arch` when no host triplet is already set, and, when `tools.android:ndk_path` is configured, populate host tool variables for `CC`, `CXX`, `LD`, `STRIP`, `RANLIB`, `AS`, `AR`, `ADDR2LINE`, `NM`, `OBJCOPY`, `OBJDUMP`, `READELF`, and `ELFEDIT`. Values already present in `VirtualBuildEnv` must take precedence over Conan-generated tool paths. During cross-building, build-side compiler executables configured through `tools.build:compiler_executables` should still be exposed as `CC_FOR_BUILD` and `CXX_FOR_BUILD`.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, `GnuToolchain` should behave consistently with the GNU/autotools-oriented toolchain flow: Apple-specific compiler and linker flags are propagated correctly, Android cross-builds auto-wire the expected NDK tools, user customizations in the build environment are preserved, and native build-machine compilers remain available separately from host-target compilers.

constraints.grounded: Do not require `tools.android:ndk_path` solely to determine the Android host triplet. Do not overwrite tool variables that are already defined by `VirtualBuildEnv`. Do not replace an explicitly established host triplet. Preserve the separation between host compiler variables and `CC_FOR_BUILD` / `CXX_FOR_BUILD` during cross-building.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve generated toolchain behavior without forcing new Android configuration just to identify the target, without clobbering user-provided environment settings, and without mixing native build-machine tools with target-host tools.

behavior: `GnuToolchain` now incorporates the Apple extra flag behavior expected from recent `AutotoolsToolchain` updates, so Apple-targeted generated compile and link flags reflect relevant Apple configuration.
For Android cross-builds, the host triplet is auto-derived from the target architecture when the host triplet is unset, even if no NDK path is configured.

When `tools.android:ndk_path` is set, `GnuToolchain` exports NDK-backed paths not only for the compiler and core binutils but also for `ADDR2LINE`, `NM`, `OBJCOPY`, `OBJDUMP`, `READELF`, and `ELFEDIT`.
Conan-generated Android tool variables are injected only when the same variables are not already supplied by the build environment, preserving user-defined `CC` and `CXX` values.

In cross-builds, build-machine compiler executables from `tools.build:compiler_executables` continue to be exposed through `CC_FOR_BUILD` and `CXX_FOR_BUILD` rather than replacing host compiler mappings.
acceptance_criteria: When generating `GnuToolchain` for an Apple target with Apple-specific toolchain configuration, the produced compiler and linker flags should reflect those Apple settings consistently with `AutotoolsToolchain`.
When cross-building to Android with a target architecture and no explicit host triplet, the generated GNU toolchain should resolve the matching Android host triplet without requiring an NDK path.

When cross-building to Android with `tools.android:ndk_path` configured, the generated environment should expose NDK-backed paths for compiler, linker, archiver, stripper, assembler, symbol, object, and ELF utility variables.
When a build environment already defines `CC` or `CXX`, generating `GnuToolchain` for Android should preserve those definitions rather than overwrite them with Conan-generated NDK compiler paths.

When `tools.build:compiler_executables` provides build-side C or C++ compilers during a cross-build, the generated environment should expose them as `CC_FOR_BUILD` and `CXX_FOR_BUILD` while keeping host tool variables separate.

task_7.title: Add opt-in no-skip requirement trait for exceptional dependency edges
task_7.description: Conan 2.16.0 adds a new `no_skip` requirement trait so recipe authors can explicitly preserve exceptional dependencies that would otherwise be skipped during graph binary analysis. This is aimed at cases such as one application privately requiring another application and still needing that transitive dependency to remain available.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that recipes can mark exceptional requirements as non-skippable so privately required application or tool dependencies that are still needed remain available instead of being skipped by Conan.

expectation.grounded: Requirement declarations must support a new `no_skip=True` trait. When Conan determines which binaries can be marked as skipped, any dependency path involving a transitive requirement flagged with `no_skip` must stay in the required set rather than being skipped, including exceptional cases where one application privately `requires` another application.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading should be able to opt specific dependency relationships out of skip pruning when those dependencies are still needed for actual package behavior, especially for wrapper-style applications or tools that privately rely on other applications.

constraints.grounded: The feature must be opt-in: requirements that do not set `no_skip=True` must continue to follow existing skip behavior. Setting `no_skip` must only affect whether dependencies are skipped and must not otherwise redefine the declared requirement relationship.
constraints.conceptual: Existing dependency behavior should remain unchanged unless a package author explicitly marks a requirement as non-skippable. The new trait should preserve needed dependencies without broadly changing how the dependency is exposed or classified.

behavior: Recipes can declare a requirement with a new `no_skip` trait, which defaults to disabled.
A requirement marked with `no_skip=True` prevents Conan from skipping the relevant dependency path during binary skip analysis, even when that path would otherwise be considered skippable.
This supports exceptional private `requires` relationships where an application or similar package depends on another application and still needs it present.
Requirements that are not marked with `no_skip=True` continue to use the prior skip behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe marks a requirement with `no_skip=True`, Conan should keep the dependency chain behind that requirement available instead of skipping it solely because it is not treated as a build or editable dependency.

When one application privately requires another application and that requirement is marked `no_skip=True`, the depended-on application should remain present for the depending package rather than being skipped.
When `no_skip` is not set on a requirement, Conan should preserve the existing skip behavior for dependencies that are otherwise eligible to be skipped.

task_8.title: Early validation for invalid conf_info value types
task_8.description: The upgrade adds early runtime validation for values assigned through `conf_info`, so Conan recipes fail immediately when they try to store raw settings or option objects as configuration values. This makes invalid configuration usage surface at the point where package metadata is produced instead of being accepted and failing later in less predictable ways.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conf_info` rejects raw Conan settings and option objects as configuration values and reports the misuse as soon as the recipe assigns them.

expectation.grounded: When a recipe uses `conf_info` to define a value or to append or prepend a single value, passing a raw `SettingsItem` or `_PackageOption` must raise a `ConanException` instead of storing that object. `conf_info` values are expected to be regular Python data values rather than Conan settings or option wrapper objects.
expectation.conceptual: Recipes should only publish configuration data through `conf_info` using normal Python values such as strings, numbers, booleans, or lists of such values. If a recipe tries to expose a live settings or options object directly, Conan should stop immediately with a clear error.

constraints.grounded: The new validation applies to `conf_info` value creation and to single-value `append()` and `prepend()` operations. Existing valid usage with regular Python types must continue to work, and the change should not alter unrelated `conf_info` composition behavior beyond rejecting these invalid object types.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to preventing invalid configuration value types. Valid `conf_info` data should behave as before, and the upgrade should not introduce new behavior changes for correctly typed configuration entries.

behavior: `conf_info` now validates assigned values at the moment a configuration entry is created.
Defining a `conf_info` entry with a raw Conan setting object is rejected with a `ConanException`.
Defining a `conf_info` entry with a raw Conan option object is rejected with a `ConanException`.
Appending a single raw Conan setting or option object to a `conf_info` entry is rejected with a `ConanException`.
Prepending a single raw Conan setting or option object to a `conf_info` entry is rejected with a `ConanException`.
The validation happens early, so the failure is surfaced during recipe execution when `package_info()` publishes configuration metadata rather than after invalid values have already been accepted.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe defines a `conf_info` entry using a plain Python value, it should continue to succeed without changing the published configuration behavior.
When a recipe defines a `conf_info` entry using a raw setting object, Conan should fail immediately with a `ConanException` instead of accepting the value.
When a recipe defines a `conf_info` entry using a raw option object, Conan should fail immediately with a `ConanException` instead of accepting the value.
When a recipe appends a single raw setting or option object to a `conf_info` entry, Conan should reject the operation with a `ConanException`.
When a recipe prepends a single raw setting or option object to a `conf_info` entry, Conan should reject the operation with a `ConanException`.
When invalid `conf_info` types are used in `package_info()`, the failure should be surfaced at that point in recipe execution rather than later in the package flow.

task_9.title: Expose former command workflows through ConanAPI
task_9.description: Conan 2.16.0 moves template generation, remote login, and build-order orchestration from CLI command implementations into ConanAPI so integrations can stop depending on private command-layer or legacy `conans` internals. The update also makes `graph info` warnings more focused by surfacing only missing or invalid package states.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that integrations upgrading to Conan 2.16.0 can perform template generation, remote authentication, and build-order operations through ConanAPI instead of command-layer internals, while preserving the existing observable behavior of those workflows and reporting `graph info` warnings only for actionable missing or invalid package states.

expectation.grounded: ConanAPI should expose programmatic entry points for the workflows previously implemented in command handlers: `new.save_template(template, defines=None, output_folder=None, force=False)`, `remotes.login(remotes, username=None, password=None)`, `graph.build_order(deps_graph, order_by='recipe', reduce=False, profile_args=None)`, and `graph.build_order_merge(files, reduce=False)`. `new.save_template` must resolve user templates before home templates and built-in templates, accept repeated `key=value` definitions, render template files, copy non-template files, default the output folder to the current working directory when none is provided, and raise `ConanException` for malformed definitions, missing templates, or overwrite attempts without `force`. `remotes.login` must authenticate each selected remote using explicit credentials when both username and password are supplied or otherwise use configured credential sources, reject a provided username when it conflicts with the resolved credential source, and return per-remote previous and current user information. `graph.build_order` and `graph.build_order_merge` must preserve build-order generation and merging behavior, including rejecting reduction without an ordering mode and refusing to merge already reduced build-order files. `graph info` must expose a warning only when graph nodes contain `Missing` or `Invalid` binaries, summarizing affected package names by category.
expectation.conceptual: The supported automation surface for these package-management workflows should be ConanAPI rather than internal CLI helpers. Consumers should be able to generate project templates, log into remotes, and compute or merge build orders programmatically with the same observable outcomes they previously got from the commands, and graph inspection should warn only about packages that are actually missing or invalid.

constraints.grounded: Do not require consumers to call private command formatter helpers or command-layer implementations to access these workflows. Existing command behavior for `conan new`, `remote login`, `graph build-order`, and build-order merge must remain materially consistent after the logic is exposed through ConanAPI. Warning output from `graph info` must not include broader dependency-graph error summaries when there are no `Missing` or `Invalid` package states.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should reduce reliance on private internals without changing the practical results of the supported workflows. Diagnostics should become narrower and more actionable, not noisier.

behavior: `ConanAPI.new.save_template()` performs the same template selection, variable parsing, rendering, file creation, overwrite checks, and non-template file copying that `conan new` previously handled in the command layer.

`ConanAPI.remotes.login()` authenticates all remotes matched by the caller, uses explicit credentials when fully provided, otherwise resolves credentials from configured sources, and fails when an explicitly requested username conflicts with the resolved credentials.
`ConanAPI.graph.build_order()` centralizes build-order creation and still rejects reduction requests that omit an ordering mode.
`ConanAPI.graph.build_order_merge()` centralizes merging of saved build-order files and rejects merge attempts for inputs that are already reduced.
`graph info` now reports warnings only for packages whose graph nodes are in `Missing` or `Invalid` binary states, grouped by those categories.
acceptance_criteria: When an integration invokes `ConanAPI.new.save_template()` with a valid template and definitions, it should generate the same rendered and copied output files that the corresponding template command would produce.

When `ConanAPI.new.save_template()` receives a malformed definition, a nonexistent template, or an existing destination file without `force`, it should fail with `ConanException` instead of partially succeeding.
When an integration invokes `ConanAPI.remotes.login()` for one or more remotes, it should authenticate each remote and return the before-and-after user association for each one.
When `ConanAPI.remotes.login()` is given a username that disagrees with the username resolved from configured credentials, it should fail rather than silently authenticating with a different user.
When an integration requests `ConanAPI.graph.build_order(..., reduce=True)` without an ordering mode, it should fail with `ConanException`.
When an integration merges build-order files through `ConanAPI.graph.build_order_merge()`, it should reject any reduced input file instead of merging it.
When `graph info` processes a graph containing missing or invalid packages, it should emit a warning that identifies the affected packages by missing and invalid categories.
When `graph info` processes a graph with neither missing nor invalid packages, it should not emit the new warning summary.

task_10.title: Public MSBuildDeps platform override for WiX x86 projects
task_10.description: Version 2.16.0 makes the MSBuild platform selection in MSBuildDeps a supported public customization point. Users can override the platform name used in generated MSBuild dependency metadata for project types such as WiX that require x86 instead of the default Win32 mapping, while default configuration and platform-key behavior remain unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that MSBuild dependency generation provides a supported way to customize the platform name used in generated property sheets so projects with nonstandard platform naming, including WiX x86 builds, can consume Conan-generated imports without platform-condition mismatches.

expectation.grounded: MSBuildDeps must expose `platform` as a supported public attribute. Its default value must be derived from `settings.arch` through the library's MSVC/MSBuild platform mapping, and consumers must be able to assign a custom platform string before generation. `configuration`, `configuration_key`, and `platform_key` must remain available with their documented default roles for selecting imported property sheets.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to rely on a public API to override the platform label used in generated MSBuild dependency metadata. If they do nothing, the library should keep using the normal architecture-based platform name; if their build system expects a different identifier, they should be able to replace it.

constraints.grounded: Default platform resolution must stay compatible with the existing MSBuild architecture mapping, including the standard `x86` to `Win32` translation unless `MSBuildDeps.platform` is explicitly overridden. Customizing `platform` must not change the default meaning of `configuration`, `configuration_key`, or `platform_key`.
constraints.conceptual: Existing builds that do not customize the platform should continue to behave the same way. The supported customization should be limited to the observable platform identifier used for MSBuild selection and should not change unrelated dependency-generation behavior.

behavior: `MSBuildDeps.platform` is part of the supported user-facing API surface.
When not overridden, `MSBuildDeps.platform` is initialized from the package architecture using the standard MSVC/MSBuild platform mapping.
For `x86` architectures, the default platform name remains `Win32`.
Consumers can override `MSBuildDeps.platform` with an alternative platform name such as `x86` before generating MSBuild dependency property sheets.
`configuration_key` and `platform_key` continue to default to `Configuration` and `Platform` for property-sheet selection.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer creates `MSBuildDeps` without overriding `platform`, generated MSBuild dependency metadata should use the default architecture-derived platform name.
When `settings.arch` is `x86` and the consumer does not override `platform`, the selected MSBuild platform should remain `Win32`.
When a consumer sets `MSBuildDeps.platform` to a custom value such as `x86` before generation, the generated MSBuild dependency metadata should use that custom value for platform-based selection.
When only `platform` is customized, configuration-based selection should continue to follow the existing `configuration`, `configuration_key`, and `platform_key` semantics.

task_11.title: Add support for newer intel-cc compiler releases
task_11.description: Conan 2.16.0 expands built-in support for Intel oneAPI C/C++ compiler releases by recognizing additional `intel-cc` version values that were previously missing. This lets users declare newer Intel compiler versions in settings while preserving the existing behavior model for the `intel-cc` compiler family.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recognizes newer `intel-cc` compiler releases so users can configure Intel oneAPI 2024.1, 2025.0, and 2025.1 in their profiles and recipes without unsupported-version failures.

expectation.grounded: The built-in `intel-cc` settings definition must accept `compiler.version` values `2024.1`, `2025.0`, and `2025.1` in addition to the previously supported releases. These versions should continue to use the existing `intel-cc` configuration surface, including the current `update`, `mode`, `libcxx`, `cppstd`, and `cstd` semantics, with no new version-specific configuration model introduced by this upgrade.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, users should be able to select recent Intel oneAPI compiler releases in Conan just like older supported `intel-cc` versions, and those selections should behave consistently with the existing Intel compiler integration.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove or alter the previously accepted `intel-cc` versions. Do not require new subsettings or change the existing configuration behavior for `intel-cc`; the upgrade should only extend the list of valid compiler releases to include the newly added versions.
constraints.conceptual: Existing Intel compiler configurations must remain compatible, and the upgrade should expand support rather than changing how the compiler family is configured.

behavior: `intel-cc` now recognizes `2024.1`, `2025.0`, and `2025.1` as valid compiler version values.
Profiles or recipes that declare one of those `intel-cc` versions are accepted by Conan's settings validation instead of being treated as unsupported compiler releases.
The newly recognized releases remain part of the same existing `intel-cc` behavior model, including the established language-standard and compiler-mode settings.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan configuration sets `compiler=intel-cc` and `compiler.version=2024.1`, it should be treated as a valid compiler setting.
When a Conan configuration sets `compiler=intel-cc` and `compiler.version=2025.0`, it should be treated as a valid compiler setting.
When a Conan configuration sets `compiler=intel-cc` and `compiler.version=2025.1`, it should be treated as a valid compiler setting.

When any of those newly supported versions is used together with existing `intel-cc` options such as compiler mode or language-standard settings, Conan should handle the configuration using the normal `intel-cc` behavior rather than requiring a separate compiler definition.
When existing supported `intel-cc` versions are used after the upgrade, their validity and configuration behavior should remain unchanged.

task_12.title: Show package configuration during source builds
task_12.description: The update adds user-visible build output that reports the effective configuration for each package as it is built from source, making it easier to understand which package-specific settings or other serialized configuration inputs are driving the build.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when packages are built from source, users can see the effective configuration being used for each package in the build output.

expectation.grounded: During a source build, Conan should emit additional package-scoped output lines that summarize the built package's serialized configuration information in a compact form. The summary should reflect the package's effective info data for that package instance and present each serialized section as a single line rather than a full expanded dump.
expectation.conceptual: When Conan builds a package from source, the user should be able to inspect the build log and immediately understand the configuration that package is being built with.

constraints.grounded: Only configuration sections that are actually present in the serialized package info should be shown. Sections represented as key-value mappings or ordered value lists should be rendered compactly, and absent or cleared sections should not produce output lines. Existing build behavior and package processing should remain unchanged apart from the added visibility in the logs.
constraints.conceptual: Show only real, effective configuration data for each built package, keep the output concise, and avoid changing the underlying build result or introducing misleading placeholders for missing values.

behavior: When Conan starts building a package from source, it emits additional output for that specific package describing its effective configuration.
The configuration is presented as compact per-section summary lines instead of a verbose full dump.
Sections whose serialized form is a mapping are shown as a section label followed by space-separated key=value entries.
Sections whose serialized form is a list are shown as a section label followed by space-separated values.
Only sections present in the package's serialized info are displayed, so unset or cleared configuration areas are omitted.
The summary is emitted separately for each package being built, allowing different packages in the same graph to show different effective configurations.
acceptance_criteria: When a package is built from source, the build output should include compact configuration summary lines for that package.
When multiple packages are built from source in the same operation, each package should show its own configuration summary in its own build log context.
When a configuration section contains multiple key-value entries, they should be shown together on one line for that section.
When a configuration section contains multiple list values, they should be shown together on one line for that section.
When a configuration field or section is not part of the package's effective serialized info, it should not appear in the build output.

task_13.title: Show per-dependency configuration in debug graph output
task_13.description: Version 2.16.0 expands dependency graph output so debug-level verbosity exposes a compact configuration summary for each dependency entry. Users can inspect what every required package is being resolved or built for without changing the default graph presentation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency graph output shown with `-vv` includes the effective configuration for each dependency entry, so users can inspect what every required, test-required, and build-required package is being built or resolved for.

expectation.grounded: When graph package output is emitted at debug verbosity (`-vv`), each dependency listed under Requirements, Test requirements, and Build requirements should keep its existing status line and additionally show indented compact configuration details for that package. The extra details should be available for listed graph entries regardless of whether their binary state is Build, Missing, Invalid, Skip, Platform, or another resolved state, and lower verbosity levels should not show them.
expectation.conceptual: Using debug-level verbose output should reveal a per-dependency configuration summary directly under each dependency in the graph, while standard verbosity continues to show only the existing dependency status lines.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove or redefine the current graph sections or the primary dependency status reporting. The added configuration details must be supplemental to the same dependency entry and gated behind debug-level verbosity only.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should add diagnostic detail without changing the structure or meaning of normal graph output, and users who do not opt into higher verbosity should not see extra output.

behavior: At `-vv`, the CLI emits one or more indented compact configuration summary lines immediately after each dependency's graph status line.
The additional configuration summary applies to regular requirements, test requirements, and build requirements shown in the dependency graph.
The configuration summary is still shown for dependency entries whose binary state is reported as built, missing, invalid, skipped, platform-resolved, or another normal graph status.
At lower verbosity levels, the dependency graph output keeps the prior level of detail and does not include the new per-dependency configuration lines.
acceptance_criteria: When a command prints a dependency graph without `-vv`, it should show the existing requirement sections and dependency status lines without extra per-dependency configuration summaries.
When a command prints a dependency graph with `-vv`, each dependency in the Requirements section should be followed by compact configuration details for that package.
When a graph includes Build requirements or Test requirements and `-vv` is enabled, those dependency entries should also include compact configuration details.

When a dependency appears in the graph with statuses such as Build, Missing, Invalid, Skip, or Platform, enabling `-vv` should still append that dependency's configuration summary after its status line.

task_14.title: Improve conan audit reporting for unscanned packages
task_14.description: The 2.16.0 update changes `conan audit` so packages missing from the vulnerability catalog are explicitly reported instead of being skipped, and provider failures are split into package-level scan errors versus fatal global errors. This makes text, JSON, and HTML reports preserve partial results and show why a package was not scanned.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan audit` explicitly reports packages that could not be scanned, continues processing remaining packages when a single package lookup fails, and still surfaces fatal provider failures after showing any partial audit results already collected.

expectation.grounded: When `conan audit` queries Conan Center or a private provider, a reference that is not found in the provider catalog should still appear in the result data for that package with a package-level error indicating that the package was not scanned. The text formatter should print that package section and show the package-level error instead of vulnerability details. The JSON formatter should emit the full structured result, including package-level errors and any global `conan_error`. The HTML formatter should render packages with no vulnerabilities and packages that were not scanned, using the package error text as the description for unscanned packages. Per-package lookup failures should not stop processing of later references, while fatal provider failures such as authentication problems, rate limiting, missing provider authentication, or HTTP request failures should remain global command errors after partial results are preserved.
expectation.conceptual: Audit reports should no longer silently omit packages that the vulnerability service cannot resolve. If one package cannot be scanned, the report should still include that package with a clear not-scanned outcome and continue auditing the rest. If the provider encounters a fatal condition that prevents the audit from continuing, the command should preserve any results gathered so far and then fail with a provider-level error.

constraints.grounded: Do not treat catalog-miss cases for an individual package as fatal command failures. Do not discard successfully collected vulnerability data for other references when one package returns a package-level error. Continue reporting successful zero-vulnerability packages as "No vulnerabilities found". Keep global provider failures distinct from package-level scan failures so clients can observe both partial data and a terminal error condition.
constraints.conceptual: Single-package lookup problems should degrade gracefully without hiding other audit results, while true provider-wide failures should still stop the command. Normal clean-scan results must remain unchanged, and the reporting model must clearly distinguish a package that was scanned successfully from one that was never scanned.

behavior: `conan audit` includes packages missing from the vulnerability catalog in its output instead of silently omitting them.
Catalog misses are represented as package-level not-scanned results for both Conan Center and private providers, and later package references continue to be processed.
Text output prints a package section for an unscanned reference and shows the package-level error rather than vulnerability entries.
HTML output renders an entry for an unscanned package and uses the not-scanned explanation as its description.
JSON output serializes the complete result object, including package entries, package-level errors, and any global `conan_error` value.

Fatal provider conditions such as authentication failure, rate limiting, internal server failure, missing provider token, or request-level exceptions are surfaced as global errors after any partial results already gathered.
acceptance_criteria: When a requested package reference is absent from the vulnerability catalog, `conan audit` should still include that package in the report and mark it as not scanned instead of omitting it.
When one package lookup fails with a package-specific catalog-miss condition but later package references are valid, the command should continue and report the later packages as usual.
When a package scans successfully and has no vulnerabilities, the report should indicate that no vulnerabilities were found for that package rather than treating it as an error.
When JSON output is requested, the result should include structured entries for each processed package and expose any fatal provider failure separately as a global error field.
When HTML output is requested, packages that were not scanned should still appear in the rendered report with a description explaining that they were not scanned.
When a fatal provider failure occurs after some packages have already been processed, the command should preserve the partial audit results collected so far and then fail with a provider-level error.

task_15.title: Fix audit HTML severity sorting and layout
task_15.description: Conan 2.16.0 adjusts the HTML vulnerability audit output so severity sorting reflects severity rank instead of display ordering, ensures entries with unknown severity do not appear ahead of ranked severities in descending sorts, and keeps the severity column rendering from overflowing the table layout.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the HTML vulnerability audit report orders rows by actual severity rank, places vulnerabilities with unknown severity below ranked severities when sorting descending, and renders the severity column without content overflow.

expectation.grounded: In the audit HTML output produced by the vulnerabilities formatter, each vulnerability row should expose a sortable severity value independently from the visible severity text. Vulnerabilities with a defined severity should continue to render a visible severity badge using the severity label, while vulnerabilities whose severity is `N/A` or empty should render as plain text. For sorting purposes, `N/A` must be treated as lower than any defined severity so descending severity order does not place those rows first.
expectation.conceptual: The HTML audit report should sort vulnerabilities by meaningful severity rather than by the presentation text. Unknown-severity items should sort after real severity levels, and the severity column should display cleanly within the report layout.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the visible severity label for known severities and preserve plain-text display for unknown or empty severities. The sort-only severity value must not change the user-visible label and must not cause `N/A` rows to outrank rows with defined severities in descending ordering.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the report appearance consistent for visible severity labels while correcting sort behavior. The fix must improve ordering and layout without changing the meaning of displayed severity information.

behavior: The severity column includes a hidden sortable value separate from the visible severity badge or text.
Rows whose severity is `N/A` sort below rows with defined severities by using a lower severity ordering value.
Defined severities continue to appear as styled severity badges showing the severity label.
Unknown or empty severities continue to appear as plain text instead of a severity badge.
Separating the sort metadata from the visible badge/text prevents the severity column content from overflowing the HTML table layout.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sorts the HTML audit report by severity in descending order, vulnerabilities with defined severities should appear before vulnerabilities whose severity is `N/A`.
When a vulnerability has a defined severity, the HTML report should display that severity as a badge while still sorting according to its severity rank.
When a vulnerability severity is `N/A` or empty, the HTML report should display the text value without a badge and should not be ranked ahead of defined severities in descending sorting.
When viewing the HTML audit table, the severity column content should remain contained within the table instead of overflowing the column.

task_17.title: Restrict saved audit provider file permissions
task_17.description: Conan 2.16.0 hardens persistence of audit provider configuration by saving the audit provider registry with owner-only read and write permissions, reducing exposure of stored provider details such as private access tokens without changing the audit provider workflow itself.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that persisted audit provider configuration is stored with access limited to the current user so sensitive provider data is not left readable or writable by other users.

expectation.grounded: When Conan saves `audit_providers.json`, the resulting file should have permissions equivalent to `0o600`, so only the file owner can read and write it. This permission hardening applies whenever the audit provider registry is written and must not change the saved provider data format or the normal audit provider management flow.
expectation.conceptual: Whenever audit provider settings are persisted, the configuration file should be secured as a private user-owned file. Users should be able to continue managing audit providers normally, while stored credentials and provider metadata are no longer exposed through overly broad filesystem permissions.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the JSON content structure, provider serialization behavior, or the success path for saving audit provider definitions beyond enforcing owner-only read/write access on the written file.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should tighten file privacy without changing how users add, update, or use audit providers, and without altering the configuration data they expect Conan to store.

behavior: Saving the audit provider registry now applies owner-only read and write permissions to `audit_providers.json`.
If `audit_providers.json` is newly created or overwritten during a save, its effective permissions are restricted to `0o600` after the write completes.
The contents of the persisted provider registry remain the same as before; only the filesystem visibility of the saved file changes.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan persists audit provider configuration, it should create or update the configuration file so that only the current user has read and write access to it.
When an existing audit provider configuration file is rewritten, it should end the operation with owner-only permissions rather than retaining broader access.
When users add or modify audit providers, the saved configuration data should remain valid and usable while the file itself becomes private to the owning user.

task_16.title: Improve audit HTML report ordering and text layout
task_16.description: Version 2.16.0 improves the usability of the audit HTML output by keeping long vulnerability descriptions contained within the report table and by aligning descending severity ordering with user expectations so unrated entries do not appear ahead of rated vulnerabilities.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the audit HTML output remains readable when vulnerability descriptions are long, and ensure that descending severity ordering presents rated vulnerabilities before entries with unavailable severity information.

expectation.grounded: The audit HTML report for vulnerabilities should render table content without description text overflowing outside its column. Long text should remain wrapped within the table cell, with the description column given sufficient visible space relative to package, identifier, severity, and score columns. When the report is ordered by descending severity, vulnerabilities with defined severities should appear ahead of packages whose severity is unavailable or shown as N/A.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to open the audit HTML report and read long vulnerability descriptions without broken table formatting, and sorting by highest severity should prioritize entries that actually have a severity over unknown or unavailable ones.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve the existing audit HTML report structure and continue to expose the same vulnerability fields in the table. It must improve text containment and ordering behavior without changing the meaning of reported vulnerability data or removing entries with unavailable severity values.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should make the report clearer and better ordered without hiding data, changing what vulnerabilities are reported, or requiring users to adopt a different reporting workflow.

behavior: The audit HTML vulnerability table uses a bounded column layout so each field remains within the table width instead of expanding unpredictably.
Long description content wraps inside its table cell rather than overflowing past the cell or breaking the overall table presentation.
The description field is displayed with more visible space than the package, identifier, severity, and score fields, improving readability for verbose vulnerability text.
acceptance_criteria: When an audit HTML report contains long vulnerability descriptions, the text should stay inside the description column and remain readable without spilling outside the table.
When viewing the audit HTML report, the table should remain structurally intact and readable even if multiple rows contain long unbroken or dense description text.
When the audit HTML output is sorted by descending severity, entries with known severities should be listed before entries whose severity is unavailable or marked as N/A.
When the report includes entries with unavailable severity values, those entries should still be shown in the report rather than omitted.

task_20.title: Fetch SCM commits explicitly before Conan Git checkout
task_20.description: Conan 2.16.0 updates the Git SCM checkout flow so recipes using conandata-based source coordinates can resolve and check out commits that are not fetched by a default clone, such as detached or pull-request-generated commits on some hosting platforms.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that recipes using Conan's Git SCM integration can retrieve and check out the commit recorded in `conandata.yml` even when that commit is not included in the refs obtained by a normal clone.

expectation.grounded: `conan.tools.scm.Git.checkout_from_conandata_coordinates()` should clone the repository referenced by `conan_data["scm"]`, explicitly fetch the configured `commit` from the `origin` remote, and then check out that commit so source retrieval works for commits that are not already present after clone.
expectation.conceptual: When a recipe restores sources from stored SCM coordinates, Conan should reliably obtain the exact requested commit before checkout, including commits that exist on the remote but are not reachable through the branch or tag refs fetched by default.

constraints.grounded: The behavior must remain compatible with existing `scm` entries that provide `url` and `commit`, continue checking out the exact requested revision, and not regress repositories where the commit is already available after clone.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should preserve normal SCM checkout behavior for existing recipes while adding support for less common remote commit layouts, without changing the intended source revision that users receive.

behavior: `Git.checkout_from_conandata_coordinates()` now performs an explicit fetch of the configured commit from `origin` before attempting checkout.
Recipes using conandata SCM coordinates can resolve commits that were created remotely but are not included in the refs downloaded by a standard clone.
If the requested commit is already present locally after clone, the additional fetch should not change the checked-out revision and should behave as a harmless compatibility step.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan_data["scm"]` contains a repository URL and commit, invoking `Git.checkout_from_conandata_coordinates()` should leave the working tree checked out at that exact commit.

When the requested commit exists on the remote but is not available from the refs fetched by a default clone, `Git.checkout_from_conandata_coordinates()` should still obtain and check out that commit successfully.

When the requested commit is already available locally after clone, `Git.checkout_from_conandata_coordinates()` should continue to complete successfully and produce the same checked-out revision as before.

task_18.title: Correct Apple SDK version settings
task_18.description: Conan 2.16.0 corrects the built-in Apple platform settings catalog so released Apple OS and SDK versions are represented accurately. The update adds missing valid versions and removes bogus SDK version entries, which changes which Apple profile and command-line setting values are accepted during configuration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Apple platform configuration only exposes real released OS and SDK versions, so users can select missing legitimate versions and cannot continue using bogus SDK version values in Conan settings.

expectation.grounded: Conan's built-in Apple settings should accept the corrected values for `settings.os.version` and `settings.os.sdk_version`. `visionOS` should include `1.3` in `settings.os.version`. `settings.os.sdk_version` should accept the newly available values `iOS=13.3`, `watchOS=7.3`, `tvOS=13.3`, `tvOS=14.4`, `tvOS=15.5`, `visionOS=1.3`, `Macos=11.2`, and `Macos=12.4`. It should no longer accept the removed bogus values `iOS=18.3`, `watchOS=11.3`, `tvOS=13.1`, `tvOS=18.3`, `visionOS=2.3`, and `Macos=15.3` for `settings.os.sdk_version`.
expectation.conceptual: Apple-related Conan settings should reflect actual released Apple platform versions. Valid released versions that were missing should become selectable, and non-existent SDK versions should no longer be treated as valid configuration choices.

constraints.grounded: Do not change unrelated Apple OS families, SDK names, or valid version entries that remain in the built-in settings catalog. Existing support for `null` SDK version values and other unchanged Apple version values must remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing Apple configuration behavior stable except for correcting the affected version lists. Users with already valid Apple settings outside the corrected entries should see no behavior change.

behavior: Conan now recognizes `visionOS` version `1.3` as a valid built-in OS version.
Conan now recognizes previously missing released Apple SDK versions: `iOS` `13.3`, `watchOS` `7.3`, `tvOS` `13.3`, `14.4`, and `15.5`, `visionOS` `1.3`, and `Macos` `11.2` and `12.4`.
Conan no longer recognizes the bogus Apple SDK versions `iOS` `18.3`, `watchOS` `11.3`, `tvOS` `13.1` and `18.3`, `visionOS` `2.3`, and `Macos` `15.3` in `settings.os.sdk_version`.
Profiles, recipes, or command-line invocations that rely on removed bogus SDK version values must now be treated as invalid and updated to a real released SDK version.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures Conan with `settings.os=visionOS` and `settings.os.version=1.3`, it should be accepted as a valid built-in setting value.

When a user configures Conan with one of the newly added Apple SDK versions (`iOS` `13.3`, `watchOS` `7.3`, `tvOS` `13.3`, `14.4`, or `15.5`, `visionOS` `1.3`, `Macos` `11.2` or `12.4`), it should be accepted as a valid built-in `settings.os.sdk_version` value.

When a user configures Conan with a removed bogus Apple SDK version (`iOS` `18.3`, `watchOS` `11.3`, `tvOS` `13.1` or `18.3`, `visionOS` `2.3`, or `Macos` `15.3`), Conan should reject it as an invalid built-in `settings.os.sdk_version` value.
When a user configures Conan with Apple SDK version values that remain valid and were not changed by this update, those values should continue to be accepted.

task_21.title: Add ARM64EC support to Microsoft build helpers
task_21.description: The update adds missing ARM64EC platform support across Conan's Microsoft and Visual Studio integration so ARM64EC targets are mapped consistently in generated MSBuild, MSBuildDeps, MSBuildToolchain, Visual Studio CMake generator, and Visual Studio layout behavior. It also aligns the generated MSBuild command-line form so the emitted invocation uses the executable name and dash-prefixed options consistently.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's Microsoft build integrations recognize and propagate the `arm64ec` architecture as a valid Visual Studio/MSBuild platform so users can generate, configure, and invoke Windows builds targeting ARM64EC without missing-platform failures or incorrect platform selection.

expectation.grounded: When `settings.arch=arm64ec`, the Microsoft-facing helpers should resolve the platform as `ARM64EC` wherever Conan derives Visual Studio or MSBuild platform names, including `MSBuild`, `MSBuildDeps`, `MSBuildToolchain`, `vs_layout`, and Visual Studio generator handling in the CMake toolchain. `MSBuild.command()` should emit an `msbuild.exe` invocation whose configuration, platform, and verbosity arguments use the normalized dash-prefixed MSBuild option form. Existing handling for `x86`, `x86_64`, `armv7`, `armv8`, and Windows CE platform selection should remain intact.
expectation.conceptual: Users targeting ARM64EC should see Conan treat that architecture as a first-class Visual Studio/MSBuild platform across project generation, dependency property sheets, layout selection, and build command creation. Generated MSBuild invocations should remain valid and consistently formatted, while existing supported Windows architectures continue to behave the same.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress the existing Visual Studio/MSBuild platform mappings for `x86`, `x86_64`, `armv7`, or `armv8`. Preserve the special Windows CE behavior that takes the platform from `settings.os.platform` in `MSBuild`. The change should affect observable platform resolution and command generation only; it should not alter unrelated build settings or require users to change their public Conan configuration model.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add ARM64EC coverage without changing how previously supported Windows targets are selected. It should keep established Windows-specific behavior working and avoid introducing unrelated build configuration changes.

behavior: Conan maps `settings.arch=arm64ec` to the Visual Studio/MSBuild platform name `ARM64EC`.
The `MSBuild` helper uses `ARM64EC` as its `Platform` value when building for `arm64ec`.
The `MSBuildDeps` generator uses `ARM64EC` in its platform-conditioned property sheet selection for `arm64ec`.
The `MSBuildToolchain` generator includes `ARM64EC` in the configuration/platform condition used for generated MSBuild properties.
Visual Studio generator handling in the CMake toolchain resolves `arm64ec` to `ARM64EC` when deriving the generator platform.
The Visual Studio layout helper accepts `arm64ec` as a supported architecture and derives the build directory layout from the `ARM64EC` platform name instead of treating it as unsupported.
Generated MSBuild command lines are emitted as `msbuild.exe` invocations using dash-prefixed property and verbosity options.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan build uses `settings.arch=arm64ec` with Microsoft tooling, generated MSBuild platform values should resolve to `ARM64EC` instead of being absent or unsupported.
When `MSBuildDeps` or `MSBuildToolchain` generate Visual Studio/MSBuild metadata for `arm64ec`, the resulting configuration should be conditioned on platform `ARM64EC`.
When Conan derives the platform for a Visual Studio CMake generator and `settings.arch=arm64ec`, it should select `ARM64EC`.
When `vs_layout` is used with `settings.arch=arm64ec`, it should produce an ARM64EC-based layout rather than rejecting the architecture as unsupported.
When `MSBuild.command()` generates the build command, it should invoke `msbuild.exe` and use normalized dash-prefixed option syntax for configuration, platform, and verbosity.
When existing supported architectures such as `x86`, `x86_64`, `armv7`, and `armv8` are used, their Visual Studio/MSBuild platform resolution should remain unchanged.

task_22.title: Expose build_args for editable packages in graph build-order
task_22.description: Conan 2.16.0 fixes `conan graph build-order` so editable dependencies that are scheduled to build are reported with actionable `build_args` in JSON output, aligning them with normal buildable packages and making build-order results usable for editable workflows.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan graph build-order` includes usable build arguments for editable packages that must be built, so users can consume build-order output consistently for both editable and non-editable dependencies.

expectation.grounded: When `conan graph build-order` emits JSON, entries whose binary status is `EditableBuild` must expose `build_args` just like entries in `Build` status. This applies to both recipe-ordered and configuration-ordered output, and the generated arguments must remain context-aware for host requirements versus tool requirements.
expectation.conceptual: Users should receive the same actionable rebuild instructions for editable dependencies that they already receive for regular packages when those dependencies appear in build-order results as needing a build.

constraints.grounded: Do not add `build_args` for binary states other than buildable ones. Existing behavior for `Build` entries must remain unchanged, and output structure compatibility for the supported `--order-by` modes must be preserved.
constraints.conceptual: Only dependencies that are actually scheduled for a build should gain build instructions, and the fix must not alter existing build-order behavior for packages that are not being built.

behavior: `conan graph build-order` JSON output now includes `build_args` for packages reported as `EditableBuild`.
The `build_args` field is generated in both package-oriented and configuration-oriented build-order output.
Editable package build arguments follow the same requirement-context rules as standard build entries, distinguishing normal requirements from tool requirements.
acceptance_criteria: When an editable dependency appears in `conan graph build-order` as needing a build, the JSON result should include a non-empty `build_args` field for that entry.
When build-order output is requested with recipe-based ordering, editable build entries should include `build_args`.
When build-order output is requested with configuration-based ordering, editable build entries should include `build_args`.
When a package is not in a buildable binary state, the command should not start emitting `build_args` for it solely because of this change.

task_19.title: Decouple Conan CLI commands from legacy imports
task_19.description: Conan 2.16.0 removes remaining runtime dependence on legacy `conans` modules inside the CLI layer so core command workflows continue to operate after those compatibility imports are no longer available. The update preserves remote authentication, graph reporting and build-order output, list timestamp rendering, profile detection output, and graph export behavior, while making graph-info warnings explicitly identify missing and invalid packages.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan CLI workflows remain usable after legacy `from conans` imports are removed, including remote authentication, graph reporting and build-order commands, profile detection output, list timestamp display, and graph export rendering.

expectation.grounded: The `conan.cli` command layer must execute `remote login`, `graph build-order`, `graph build-order-merge`, `graph info`, graph HTML/DOT formatting, `list`, and `profile detect` without requiring legacy `from conans` imports. `remote login` must authenticate all remotes matched by the requested pattern and still raise `ConanException` when no remotes match. `graph info` must keep surfacing graph errors separately and also expose a warning that lists package names whose binary state is `Missing` or `Invalid`. Human-readable timestamps in `list` output must be rendered in UTC. `profile detect` must create missing parent directories before writing the detected profile.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to 2.16.0 should be able to keep using the same Conan CLI commands even if old compatibility modules are unavailable. Remote login, build-order generation, graph inspection and export, profile detection, and package-list timestamp output should continue to work, and graph inspection should clearly call out packages that are missing binaries or are invalid.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the observable contracts of the existing CLI entry points: build-order commands must keep returning serialized build-order data together with surfaced graph errors, `list` must continue emitting human-readable revision timestamps in UTC, graph exports must still render, `profile detect` must still write to explicit output paths, and `remote login` must continue processing all remotes matched by the pattern. The change must not require legacy import paths or new command syntax.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the upgrade backward-compatible for normal CLI usage. Removing the old compatibility dependency must not break established command invocations, hide dependency problems, or force users to change how they specify remotes, graph inputs, profiles, or list queries.

behavior: Running `conan remote login` with a matching remote pattern authenticates each matched remote; running it with no matches raises `ConanException`.
Running `conan graph build-order` or `conan graph build-order-merge` returns serialized build-order information and any surfaced graph errors without depending on legacy graph imports.
Running `conan graph info` on a graph that contains `Missing` or `Invalid` binaries emits a warning summary naming the affected packages.
Dependency graph errors remain a separate error signal from the warning summary returned by `conan graph info`.
`conan list` text and compact outputs render revision timestamps as human-readable UTC times.
`conan profile detect` writes the detected profile even when the requested output path includes parent directories that do not yet exist.
Graph HTML and DOT formatters continue to render from serialized graph data even when legacy compatibility imports are unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: When legacy `conans` compatibility imports are absent, the affected `conan.cli` commands should still run and produce normal command output instead of import-time failures.
When `conan remote login <pattern>` matches one or more remotes, it should authenticate those remotes; when it matches none, it should report a `ConanException`.

When `conan graph info` evaluates a graph containing packages in `Missing` or `Invalid` states, it should return a warning that names those packages, while any graph error remains separately reported.
When users request build-order generation or merge, the CLI should still return serialized build-order data together with surfaced graph errors.
When `conan list` shows revision timestamps in human-readable output, it should display UTC timestamps.
When `conan profile detect` writes to a nested output path, it should create any missing parent directories and produce the profile file.
When users export graph output as HTML or DOT, it should render successfully without depending on legacy compatibility imports.

task_23.title: Clarify private audit provider curation errors
task_23.description: The upgrade improves how Conan reports private audit provider failures. When a private provider is backed by a JFrog Platform instance without JFrog Curation, users should receive an explicit warning about the likely cause instead of a generic wrapped error, and package-not-found responses should be described as packages not being scanned rather than catalog lookup failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that private audit provider failures explain when JFrog Curation is likely unavailable, and ensure that package-not-found audit results are reported as packages not scanned rather than as vague or misleading provider errors.
